methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $105M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
EarthGrid is a Seed-stage transportation company that has raised $105.3M to date. The broader transportation sector comprises six private peers of varying maturity (including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Navier, and Olympian Motors) and no public comparables. No sufficiently narrow peer set exists at the same stage and valuation tier to support a reliable median-based valuation.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable triangulation method. Using total capital raised as a proxy base value of $105M and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier for progression from Seed to the next financing round yields an implied valuation of $263M. This method assumes EarthGrid's capital efficiency and dilution patterns track sector norms; sensitivity analysis around the multiplier produces a low bound of $224M (2.1x) and a high bound of $303M (2.9x).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $224M to $303M, centered on $263M. Material uncertainties include the representativeness of the 2.5x step-up multiplier given EarthGrid's specific burn rate, product maturity, and market traction—none of which are quantified in the available data. Additionally, the absence of a comparable peer set limits cross-validation. Refinement would benefit from access to subsequent-round comparable pricing and EarthGrid's detailed financial trajectory.
